articles.headline: NBA transaction glossary: Trade, free agency, extension, CBA terms to know
articles.description: The world of NBA transactions is often difficult to decipher. Our resident GM is here to help.﻿
articles.body:
The world of NBA transactions -- with its two aprons, trade exceptions, Bird rights and all -- is often difficult to decipher. We're here to help.

From the basics of the league's collective bargaining agreement to the finest details of the salary cap, let's run through the most important terms you'll see on ESPN during the run-up to the trade deadline, the draft and free agency.

Jump to a section:

Basics | Roster rules | Salary cap and taxes

Apron | Free agency | Cap, trade exceptions

Extension types | Two-way, 10-day contracts

The basics

Collective bargaining agreement (CBA): A legal contract between the NBA and the National Basketball Players Association (NBPA), covering various aspects of league operations, including player salaries, revenue sharing and the salary cap. The current CBA was ratified ahead of the 2023-24 season and expired after the 2029-30 campaign. (Either side can opt out of the agreement for the 2029-30 season if written notice is provided by Oct. 15, 2028.)

Salary cap: The leaguewide limit on total player salaries ($165.0 million for 2026-27). Teams over the salary cap can add players only through exceptions or trades that match outgoing money.

Luxury tax: A higher threshold above the salary cap ($200.4 million for 2026-27). Teams in the luxury tax face penalties on every dollar above the line and have a smaller midlevel exception.

Aprons: Thresholds above the luxury tax line that trigger additional restrictions on team spending and roster-building. First apron for 2026-27: $209 million. Second apron for 2026-27: $221.7 million

Salary cap exceptions: Rules allowing teams to exceed the salary cap in specific scenarios, such as re-signing players with "Bird rights" or signing new players using the midlevel, biannual and minimum exceptions.

Trade exceptions: Created when a team trades a player. For teams under the aprons, the expanded traded player exception can bring in more salary than is sent out. For example, if Team A trades a player earning $14 million to Team B for a player earning $6 million, Team A will create an $8 million trade exception.

If a team acquires a player for a lesser salary than what is sent out, it unlocks the standard traded player exception -- used to acquire a player within a year, earning up to $250,000 more than the exception. Sign-and-trade: A contract mechanism in which players sign with their current team and are immediately traded. This requires a minimum three-year contract, with the first year guaranteed.

Teams above the aprons cannot acquire a player via sign-and-trade, and teams above the second apron can send out a player via sign-and-trade but cannot use that outgoing salary to bring back any in return.

Veteran minimum contracts: One- or two-year contracts based on a scale issued annually on June 30 by the NBA. If a player signs for one year at the minimum and has more than two years of service, their higher salary is treated as if they had signed as a veteran with two years

articles.headline: What's working -- and not working -- for LeBron James, Philadelphia 76ers
articles.description: We talked to several coaches, executives and scouts about the 11-3 Sixers in an attempt to get a consensus opinion on their start.
articles.body:
There are few people on the planet more qualified to speak about what it's like to be a part of a nascent LeBron James-led group with immediate super-team expectations than former NBA sharpshooter Mike Miller.

As a member of the Miami Heat for the first three years of the Heatles' run (2010-13) who again teamed up with James for the tumultuous first season of the superstar's second stint with the Cleveland Cavaliers (2014-15), Miller knows life in the LeBron pressure cooker.

"Everywhere he went, you would find out real quickly who's going to be able to step out there and who's not," said Miller, who now is an agent representing NBA players as the president of LIFT Sports Management. "It's different. Every shot now, crowd-wise, everything becomes magnified. I've had some good success personally [before playing with James], but nothing on the level of where you really test yourself on that stage.

"That's the reason I chose Miami. I wanted to know if I was going to s--- myself, or perform?"

So far, for the most part, the Philadelphia 76ers have performed fantastically.

The Sixers won eight of their first nine games, including an opening-night victory at Madison Square Garden to spoil the New York Knicks' ring night. They came back from down 29 points to beat the Cavaliers. And they went on the road to avenge a previous loss to the Detroit Pistons, last season's No. 1 seed in the Eastern Conference.

But two blowout losses in their last four games in Cleveland -- when James and Joel Embiid combined to shoot 3-for-21 and had eight turnovers -- and at home against their longtime rivals in the Boston Celtics -- which caused Jaylen Brown to admit afterward how frustrated he was by his showing -- brought them back down to earth.

With nearly a sixth of the season complete, ESPN talked to several coaches, executives and scouts about the 11-3 Sixers in an attempt to answer four big questions and get a consensus opinion on their start and what to expect the rest of the way.

Jump to a question:

How does this start compare to others?

What's fueling this 76ers' 11-3 run?

Do they have flexibility to make additions?

Are they a legit title contender?

Why is this start different than James' first season in Miami, second stop in Cleveland and first season in L.A.?

When James took his talents to South Beach in 2010, he was 25 and coming off back-to-back MVP seasons. He was at his physical peak and eager to get over the championship hump that had eluded him his first seven years with the Cavs.

When he went back to Cleveland in 2014, he was universally crowned the league's best player, coming off four straight trips to the NBA Finals and winning two titles, two Finals MVPs and two more regular-season MVPs with Miami.

When James got to L.A. in 2018 -- now having been to eight straight Finals -- he was in full command of his game but was 34 years old with a ton of minutes on his body.

Now in Philadelphia, the 41-year-old James isn't close to being consider

articles.headline: Meet Como's Nico Paz, the heir to Lionel Messi's Argentina No. 10 shirt
articles.description: Como's Nico Paz has become one of the best young players in Europe, but now he faces the unenviable task of stepping into Lionel Messi's Argentina No. 10 shirt.
articles.body:
Como's Nico Paz has become one of the best young players in Europe this season, but now he faces the unenviable task of stepping into the Argentina No. 10 shirt worn by the legendary Lionel Messi.

Paz is the son of Pablo Paz, who played for Argentina at the 1998 World Cup, and was born in Tenerife, Spain. He began his senior career at Real Madrid and spent three years with their B team, RM Castilla, but struggled to break into the first team. He made his debut in January 2022 -- and his international debut came a few months later -- yet only managed eight first-team appearances in all competitions before leaving for Como in August 2024 for around €6 million, though his contract included various clauses allowing Madrid to re-sign him.

Under former Barcelona, Arsenal and Chelsea midfielder Cesc Fàbregas, himself in his first senior coaching job at Como, Paz developed incredibly. "He taught me practically everything," Paz told UEFA earlier this year. "I arrived here as a young player from Castilla. I'd played a few games for Real Madrid, but in the end I was a reserve-team player in a lower division.

"Coming here and playing in Serie A, the top flight, allowed me to grow and improve a lot, both as a player and as a person. It was all thanks to Cesc, who believed in me and brought me here. From the first day he let me play the way I wanted and gave me a lot of freedom. He taught me a lot. I think the player I am today is all down to him."

His form for Como took off and he has scored 25 goals and made 25 assists in his 89 games so far -- six goals and eight assists from 14 games this season. Obviously that saw plenty of transfer links, including to Arsenal and Chelsea, but a complicated deal saw Madrid agree to let Como take on his full rights for around €60 million this summer, with a clause for them to re-sign the player for €80 million in 2027 if they wish.

So who is Argentina's heir to Messi, now that the great man has retired from international football? And what do we need to know about his style of play? Sam Tighe and Tor-Kristian Karlsen explore.

Can Nico Paz replace Lionel Messi for Argentina?

Comparing anyone to arguably the greatest player the world has ever seen can feel cruel, but it's a rite of passage any young creative Argentine player must undertake -- particularly in the wake of Messi's international retirement and the fact that Paz will take over his No. 10 shirt.

In the seasons they turned 21 (and played a full campaign), Messi racked up 34 league goals contributions for Barcelona in 2008-09 -- the season that saw Barcelona win the Champions League and Messi score in the 2-0 win in the final. That split into 23 goals and 11 assists, and he overperformed his expected goals tally (11.85) by a huge margin.

articles.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Man United eye USMNT's McKennie amid Pochettino arrival
articles.description: Incoming Manchester United boss Mauricio Pochettino is eyeing a quick reunion with USMNT midfielder Weston McKennie. Transfer Talk has the latest.
articles.body:
Incoming Manchester United boss Mauricio Pochettino is eyeing a quick reunion with USMNT midfielder Weston McKennie, while Atlético Madrid are exploring a deal for Lisandro Martínez.

Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Manchester United are interested in United States men's national team midfielder Weston McKennie, according to La Gazzetta dello Sport. Incoming head coach Mauricio Pochettino admires the 28-year-old's versatility after working with him with the USMNT and could seek a reunion at Old Trafford. However, McKennie's club, Juventus, see him as central to head coach Luciano Spalletti's plans and are reluctant to sanction a January departure. His contract runs until June 2030.

- Fulham defender Calvin Bassey is expected to feature prominently among Manchester United's January targets under Pochettino, according to The Telegraph. The incoming head coach wants to strengthen his backline, with Bassey's pace and ability to cover at full back making him an attractive option. The Nigeria international's contract runs until next summer, although Fulham hold an option to extend it by a further 12 months.

- Chelsea continue to track Kerim Alajbegović, having come close to signing him before his summer move to Juventus, La Gazzetta dello Sport has revealed. The Serie A giants are determined to resist any efforts to lure him away from Turin. Alajbegović, 19, is contracted until 2031 and remains -- much like McKennie -- a key member of Spalletti's Juve squad. At this stage, no formal negotiations have taken place between the two clubs.

- Atlético Madrid are exploring a January move for Manchester United defender Lisandro Martínez, as per TEAMtalk. Diego Simeone's side are attracted by the prospect of pairing the 28-year-old with his Argentine teammate Cristian Romero, although Barcelona are also interested. Martínez has indicated he wants to leave United in 2027 and favours a move to Spain, with the Premier League club open to his departure as they look to reshape their squad.

- Brighton & Hove Albion, Bayer Leverkusen and RB Leipzig are pursuing Juventus midfielder Adin Licina ahead of January, Tuttosport reports. The teenager is on loan at Cremonese, and Juventus remain reluctant to let him leave permanently before assessing his potential at Serie A level. Bayern Munich retain a preferential right and a 30% share of any future transfer fee.

OTHERS

- Everton are among the clubs interested in Flamengo winger Samuel Lino. The 26-year-old Brazilian is also attracting attention from Roma, Napoli, Juventus and Paris Saint-Germain, although Flamengo view him as an important part of their plans. (4-4-2 via Liverpool Echo)

articles.headline: Mauricio Pochettino to Man United: Is Tottenham love affair finally over?
articles.description: Mauricio Pochettino is back in the Premier League as the new Man United boss. For Tottenham fans, it's complicated.
articles.headlineJa: マウリシオ・ポチェッティーノがマンUへ：トッテナムとの愛の物語はついに終わるのか？
articles.descriptionJa: マウリシオ・ポチェッティーノがマンチェスター・ユナイテッドの新監督としてプレミアリーグに復帰します。トッテナムのファンにとっては、複雑な心境となるでしょう。
articles.body:
"He's magic, you know, Mauricio Pochettino!" For five years, these were the words that rang out amongst Tottenham fans.

First, at the old White Hart Lane -- a much-loved, if dilapidated, ground that became a fortress during Pochettino's years as head coach of the club. Then, at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium -- a magnificent arena that, in recent years, has felt more like a house of horrors than any sort of stronghold.

But now Pochettino is back in the Premier League, this time as Manchester United manager. And for Tottenham fans who once dreamed of seeing the Argentine return to north London, it's another reminder that the man who gave us so many unforgettable memories might never be coming home.

The Pochettino love affair

The Argentine manager joined Tottenham in 2014 and was at the helm of one of the best, and most beloved, Spurs teams in the club's history. Under Pochettino, Harry Kane (now a Ballon d'Or winner!), Son Heung-Min, Christian Eriksen, Dele Alli, Jan Vertonghen, Toby Alderweireld, Mousa Dembélé and Hugo Lloris all shone in ways that few football fans and pundits expected.

During the Pochettino era, Tottenham came agonisingly close to winning the Premier League and reached the Champions League final. They went an entire season unbeaten at home -- somewhat unthinkable now given the team's struggles at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium -- and played some of the most thrilling football in the league at the time.

There were famous victories over arch-rivals Arsenal and in Europe, including over Real Madrid and Borussia Dortmund, and, of course, there was that night in Amsterdam. When Lucas Moura scored an astonishing hat trick against Ajax to send Spurs to the Champions League final for the first time in our history.

For many Spurs fans, including myself, the Poch years brought some of our best ever memories of supporting the club. There was a special connection between Pochettino and fans. He was revered and many of us hoped that it would last forever -- even if we all knew that, really, nothing ever lasts that long. Especially not in football.

When Pochettino was sacked, rather unceremoniously, in November 2019 -- just months after taking us to the Champions League final -- it felt somewhat unjust.

It was clear for anyone to see in 2019 that Tottenham's squad was beginning to get stale in a number of areas and that what the club truly needed was a rebuild. For myriad reasons, that never came to fruition and so, when, results on the pitch took a nosedive in the winter of that year the axe fell on Pochettino.

Overnight, the man who had turned Tottenham into a truly formidable side capable of beating anyone on their day was gone. Since then, it's fair to say that no other manager that has taken the wheel at the club has managed to form the same sort of bond that Pochettino had with us.

Many have come and gone but it hasn't yet felt like any of them have "got" us the way that Pochettino did. It is early days under Roberto De Zerbi

articles.headline: Joe Burrow's 4-TD night puts QB in company of Tom Brady, Peyton Manning
articles.description: Bengals QB Joe Burrow threw for 409 yards with four touchdowns and no interceptions Sunday night, becoming just the third player in NFL history after Tom Brady and Peyton Manning to throw at least 20 passing touchdowns in a five-game span.
articles.body:
CINCINNATI -- Even after a performance that was reminiscent of some of the greatest quarterbacks in NFL history and enhanced his case as the current best in the league, Joe Burrow was not in the mood to bask in his latest achievement.

During the Cincinnati Bengals' 38-18 win against the Pittsburgh Steelers, Burrow became the third player in NFL history to throw at least 20 passing touchdowns in a five-game span, according to ESPN Research. He joined Tom Brady and Peyton Manning. 

Burrow let his guard down only a couple of times after the game, including when he was asked what kind of quarterback he was Sunday night at Paycor Stadium.

"A great one," Burrow said with one of the few smiles he offered after the game.

Despite Burrow being tight-lipped after Cincinnati's fifth consecutive win, the numbers said plenty: He was 35-of-44 passing for 409 yards with four touchdowns and no interceptions.

Per Next Gen Stats, Burrow was perfect against the blitz (completed all 12 passes) and led Cincinnati to its fifth straight game scoring 30 or more points, the longest such streak in franchise history.

"I'm not watching every game, but I can promise you people who aren't talking about him aren't watching all of our games," Bengals coach Zac Taylor said. "Because if you are, it's really hard to say this dude's not the best player on planet Earth."

The Bengals (7-2) bludgeoned the Steelers from the outset. Cincinnati scored on five of its first six drives, the lone exception coming on kicker Evan McPherson's first missed field goal attempt of the season.

Against a Steelers defense that ranked fifth in fewest points allowed per drive entering Sunday (1.57), the Bengals had 337 yards by halftime and a 21-point advantage that partially illustrated Cincinnati's dominance Sunday night.

Burrow wasn't the only Bengal who had a big night. Wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase finished with 11 catches for a season-high 231 yards. He came within 26 yards of breaking his franchise record, which he set as a rookie in a 2021 win over Kansas City.

Chase has played with Burrow since they led LSU to a national championship in 2019. It's easy for Chase to see why Burrow is playing so well. 

"He's confident in his craft right now," Chase said. "He's confident his receivers will be open, and that's what you want in a quarterback."

Burrow threw two touchdown passes to running back Chase Brown, one to tight end Drew Sample and one to first-year player Dohnte Meyers, the former CFL star who caught his first career NFL TD on Sunday night.

The Bengals' win avenged a 30-27 loss to the Steelers (6-3) in Week 3, when Burrow was sacked and lost a fumble on the final offensive drive. 

Cincinnati is in sole possession of first place in the AFC North, but that didn't mean much to Burrow. 

"Nobody's winning the division with seven wins," Burrow said. "Nobody is making the playoffs with seven wins. We certainly aren't satisfied."

articles.headline: NFL Week 10: Big takeaways, questions and fantasy spin from Sunday's games
articles.description: Our NFL Nation reporters react to all the action, answering the biggest questions coming out of each Sunday game. Here's what we learned from Week 10.
articles.body:
The Sunday slate for Week 10 of the 2026 NFL season kicked off in Munich between the Patriots and Lions. Detroit improved to 7-2 with a win after the Patriots lost Drake Maye early to an ankle injury.

Back in the United States, the Vikings comfortably defeated the Packers in quarterback Kirk Cousins' first game since being traded from the Raiders. Without running back Kenneth Walker III (groin injury), the Chiefs started rookie Emmett Johnson, who coasted to 171 scrimmage yards and two touchdowns in a win over the Falcons. And the Jets went their second straight game without scoring a touchdown, losing to the Bills.

In the late window, rookie quarterbacks Carson Beck (Cardinals) and Fernando Mendoza (Raiders) made their debuts as NFL starters. Beck threw two interceptions and zero touchdowns in a loss to the Rams; Mendoza finished with a rushing score and zero turnovers in a loss to the Seahawks. Offense was not an issue in 49ers-Cowboys, as both teams combined for 86 points in a San Francisco win. Sunday night saw the Bengals put on a clinic in a blowout win over the Steelers and rise to first place in the AFC North.

Our NFL Nation reporters react to all the action, answering lingering questions coming out of each game. Fantasy football analysts Matt Bowen and Tristan Cockcroft also have fantasy takeaways from each matchup.

Let's get to it with the biggest lessons from Sunday.

Jump to:

PIT-CIN | SF-DAL | SEA-LV

LAR-ARI | HOU-CLE | MIA-IND

CAR-NO | JAX-TEN | BUF-NYJ

KC-ATL | MIN-GB | NE-DET

Catch up on Thursday's game:

WSH-NYG

Cincinnati 38, Pittsburgh 18

Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Bengals

Are the Bengals a true Super Bowl contender? With how the offense is playing, it definitely looks like it. For the first time in franchise history, Cincinnati has scored 30 or more points in five straight games. After a dazzling performance in Madrid, the Bengals carried that momentum into a big AFC North showdown at home. With quarterback Joe Burrow (35-for-44 for 409 passing yards and four TDs) playing at an MVP level and receivers Ja'Marr Chase (11 catches for 231 receiving yards) and Tee Higgins (five catches for 66 yards) also playing as well as they have in their respective careers, this offense is good enough to carry Cincinnati on a deep playoff run.

What to make of the QB performance: At this rate, Burrow will be the unquestioned front-runner to win Most Valuable Player. There was nothing he couldn't do Sunday night -- including hitting Chase in stride on multiple deep balls. Burrow is the first player since 2013 with at least 20 passing touchdowns in a five-game span. -- Ben Baby

Trending rumors

- Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes is holding off on signing a new contract for now, says The Sun. Fernandes, 32, has a contract which expires next summer -- albeit with a one-year club option to renew -- and reportedly wants to wait to see what happens under new boss Mauricio Pochettino. The Portugal midfielder has been linked with a lucrative move to Saudi Arabia before.

- Arsenal are in the market for a center forward, and TEAMtalk claims that the Gunners are the latest team to join a long list of admirers following Middlesbrough striker Will Lankshear. The 21-year-old joined Boro from Tottenham Hotspur this summer, after a loan spell at Oxford United in the Championship, and has hit the ground running, scoring 13 goals in as many appearances in the league so far. That has brought about plenty of transfer interest, but Middlesbrough will try to block any exit in January.

- Arsenal are continuing the push to sign a left-sided forward, with RB Leipzig star Antonio Nusa leading their shortlist, says TEAMtalk. Gabriel Martinelli and Leandro Trossard left in the summer, and were replaced by Christos Tzolis before a move to sign Vinícius Júnior from Real Madrid fell short. With Mikel Arteta wanting more options on that flank, the report claims that talks have opened with Nusa's representatives about a possible switch, but the 21-year-old's transfer could cost €80 million.

- Tottenham defender Pedro Porro has decided that he only wants to join Barcelona if he leaves the club, according to Sport. The 27-year-old Spain right back has seen interest from the Blaugrana, as well as Real Madrid, despite only signing a new contract with Spurs in the summer. But while Barcelona are eyeing up a deal worth no more than €50 million next summer, Tottenham will stand firm on their €70 million valuation.

- AC Milan are looking to bolster in the forward areas during January, with Gazzetta dello Sport reporting that Real Madrid's Endrick and Club Brugge's Nicolò Tresoldi are on their shortlist. articles.headline: Spain 'overwhelmed' by 'exceptional' England: We also know how to lose
articles.description: Coach Luis de la Fuente said Spain were "overwhelmed" in the early stages of Sunday's 3-2 UEFA Nations League defeat to England, but backed his team to return stronger after seeing their three-year unbeaten run come to an end.
articles.body:
Coach Luis de la Fuente said Spain were "overwhelmed" in the early stages of Sunday's 3-2 UEFA Nations League defeat to England, but backed his team to return stronger after seeing their three-year unbeaten run come to an end.

Spain trailed 3-0 at the Metropolitano before goals from Mikel Oyarzabal and Nico Williams --- both created by Lamine Yamal -- saw them come close to pulling off a dramatic comeback.

The reigning world and European champions hadn't lost a competitive game in 43 matches, but now finish second behind England in their Nations League group, meaning a tougher draw for next year's quarterfinals.

"I take away only positives [from the game]," De la Fuente said in his postmatch news conference. "It highlights just how difficult it is to reach the level we've reached.

"Just as we know how to win, we also know how to lose. It's true that we were overwhelmed in the first 30 minutes, but I really believed we would mount a comeback in the final stages."

Spain had beaten England 3-2 at Wembley in their previous meeting in September. They will find out who they'll face in the next round of the Nations League in Friday's draw in Nyon, Switzerland.

"It's a shame we have to wait until March [to play again]," De la Fuente said on Sunday. "We'll like to have another game next week. But we'll head into that knockout tie with a real desire to win."

De la Fuente refused to be critical of his team, who were second-best to an exceptional England for the first 60 minutes.

"We faced an exceptional national team today," De la Fuente said. "It only underscores the value of everything we've achieved so far.

"I'm already looking forward to the next training camp. The team is motivated to take on a new challenge."

articles.headline: Andy Burnham urges caution on potential moves to scrap Premier League 3pm blackout
articles.description: Prime Minister Andy Burnham says he would "urge caution" on scrapping the Saturday 3pm blackout.
articles.body:
Prime Minister Andy Burnham says he would "urge caution" on scrapping the Saturday 3pm blackout, and called for broadcasters to be mindful of the impact on fans caused by changes to kick-off times.

The ban on broadcasting live matches between 2.45 p.m. and 5.15 p.m on Saturdays was introduced in the 1960s but it could be dropped for the next set of Premier League, EFL and Scottish Professional Football League (SPFL) rights cycles from 2029-30.

The purpose of the blackout has been to protect live attendance at matches, amid fears crowds would be affected, especially in lower league or non-league football, if top-flight matches were available to watch on television or streaming services.

Burnham said any decision to remove the ban would require careful thought about the consequences.

"I would urge a bit of caution on it [the blackout], because it does protect the income of lower league clubs," he said.

"If you have effectively wall-to-wall Premier League football at any time, it takes away perhaps the incentive to go and watch the football league or non-league.

"So I think it has to be considered carefully. I'm not going to take the pure consumer view here. I'll take the health of football approach to this particular issue.

"I would first of all want to protect the football pyramid before I agree to saying 'let's have even more live football."

- Andy Burnham to publish Man City mayoral dealings after intervention draws criticism

- UK PM Burnham wants 'outdated' football drinking ban scrapped

"I think it's about protecting the experience with the paying supporter, protecting the football pyramid. Those issues matter to me, first of all."

The trend in television rights has been to offer more matches in order to keep revenues up -- the current Premier League deal includes 270 live matches compared to 200 in the previous one for example.

The logical conclusion of that trend is for all matches to be made available live, and the SPFL's tender for its next set of rights is reported to offer the chance to do just that.

The blackout is enforced by article 48 of UEFA's statutes, which the Football Association and the Scottish Football Association choose to impose.

It applies when 50% or more of matches in the top two divisions are due to be played simultaneously.

Premier League chief executive Richard Masters told talkSPORT in August that English football was leaning towards a blackout but added: "It's not just us involved in the decision about article 48. It's us, the EFL and the FA.

""We've got to take that decision at some point in the future about whether things are going to change.

"It's not a decision for now. It's a decision we've got to make before the next set of domestic processes that the EFL and the Premier League are going to do.

"I'd say in about 18 months time we'll come back to that decision about whether article 48 should remain or not."

articles.headline: Reaction as Brazil legend Ronaldinho comes out of retirement at Ravenna
articles.description: Ronaldinho came out of retirement to play for Italian Serie C side Ravenna at age 46 in a bid to score his 300th career goal, but couldn't manage it. Here's what happened.
articles.headlineJa: ブラジルの伝説ロナウジーニョがラヴェンナで現役復帰、周囲の反応は？
articles.descriptionJa: ロナウジーニョはキャリア300ゴール目を達成するため、46歳でイタリア・セリエCのラヴェンナに加入し現役復帰したが、目標達成には至らなかった。その詳細をレポートする。
articles.body:
Former Barcelona and AC Milan forward Ronaldinho, 46, came out of retirement on Sunday to play for Italian Serie C club Ravenna against Forli, but could only play for 45 minutes.

The Brazil legend retired on 299 career goals, with his final match for Fluminense in September 2015, and he chose a third-tier club in Italy to try and reach the magic number of 300. However, despite a few neat flicks and tricks, he was unable to get on the scoresheet.

The 2002-World Cup champion and back-to-back FIFA World Player of the Year nearly got an assist when his corner found the head of Giulio Donati, but was well saved. And he played a small part in the opening goal as he held off an opponent before the ball found its way to Donati who unleashed a shot that former Brazil defender Roberto Carlos would have been proud of.

Catch up on everything that happened.

articles.headline: Haaland 'incredibly happy' at Man City, not thinking about possible sanctions
articles.description: Erling Haaland says he is "incredibly happy" at Manchester City and his focus is on performing and not on the potential sanctions against the club.
articles.body:
Erling Haaland says he is "incredibly happy" at Manchester City and his focus is on performing and not on the potential sanctions against the club.

City have appealed after being found guilty of more than 100 breaches of the Premier League's financial regulations.

The club could face heavy sanctions, including huge points deductions or demotion, should the verdict be upheld.

Haaland was asked about the case after Norway's 3-1 Nations League victory over Wales in Oslo on Saturday night, in which he scored his 66th goal in 60 international appearances.

"This is a question I struggle to answer, because it's a legal battle between the Premier League and Manchester City," Haaland told Norwegian broadcaster TV2.

"Am I supposed to answer that? I don't really know. It's a difficult question to answer when I don't know that much about it.

"To be completely honest, I'm focused on trying to perform for Manchester City. A club I signed a five-year deal with in 2022, and a new nine-and-a-half-year deal in late 2024.

"I think that says everything about the matter. I'm a City player and I'm incredibly happy there."

Asked if the situation affects his City future, Haaland replied: "I understand that you want a little headline here, but as I said I signed a long-term contract in 2024.

"I'd say I made a pretty good choice by joining City in 2022. We can all agree on that.

"I won't say it myself, but look at the trophies I've won and how I've developed on and off the pitch.

"I'm standing here after winning an international 3-1. Things aren't going so well in the Premier League, but we'll try to turn that around against Fulham [on Saturday]."

- MrBeast, meet Haaland: Man City star puts YouTuber through soccer gauntlet

- Man City charges outcome cannot leave 'room for doubt' - sports integrity chief

City maintain they have a "comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence" to support their case, despite being found guilty by an independent commission in September.

The commission's damning findings included breaches relating to the concealment of funding worth more than £830million over a nine-year period between 2009 and 2018.

Haaland said the period under investigation happened before he joined City, and in the interview he painstakingly pointed out each stage of his football journey during that time.

He also name checked fellow Norwegian players Abdisalam Ibrahim, Martin Samuelsen, Omar Elabdellaoui and Kjetil Haug, who spent time at City during that era.

Haaland said: "The investigation covered 2009-2018. I assume the answers will come.

"I don't know when. I haven't read much about it."
